On this day in 1606, a new chapter began in Sikh history.

Guru Arjan Dev Ji, knowing that Their physical end was near, prepared the Panth for a future that would require strength alongside spirituality. Before answering the emperor’s summons to Lahore — from which They would not return — Guru Ji passed the divine light of Guruship to Their son, Sri Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.

On Jeth Vadi Ashtami (May 1606), Guru Ji called for Baba Buddha Ji and Bhai Gurdas Ji. They asked if the Sahibzada was ready. Baba Buddha Ji replied, “Your light lives within them. They will be a great warrior, a bearer of arms.”

Guru Ji stood with joy, holding a coconut and five coins. They circled Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji three times and bestowed Guruship, placing Their divine light into the young Guru. Baba Buddha Ji then applied the saffron and sandalwood tilak — the sacred mark of leadership.

Before leaving, Guru Ji entrusted the Guru’s house to five devoted Sikhs and departed for Lahore with five more — where They embraced martyrdom with unshakable peace, sitting on a burning plate as hot sand was poured upon Them.

Guru Ji’s final message:

“Do not mourn for us. Sing praises of Waheguru. Meet Guru Hargobind with joy. The time has come to rise. Take up arms. Sit upon the throne. Establish righteousness. Build an army. Destroy falsehood. Defend the truth.”

With this, the path of Miri-Piri was born — a revolution of spirit and strength.

From silence to shastar,
From sehaj to sovereignty,
From sacrifice to Sant-Sipahi.

This was not the end.
This… was Gurta Gaddi.

Join us for a glimpse into the Wednesday Sikh Ithihas class at Dashmesh Gurdwara. This week, the children shared their creative homework projects based on two beautiful sakhis (stories):
	•	One group created a large hand fan to represent the sakhi of Bhai Sai Das Ji and Bibi Ramo Ji, who lovingly fanned Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji while Guru Ji was spiritually aiding Sikhs on a boat.
	•	Another group made two rotis to depict the sakhi of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, Malik Bhago, and Bhai Lalo Ji—showing the contrast between food earned through honest living and food gained through exploitation.

Through these projects, the children learned how Sikh history continues to inspire us to live with seva (selfless service), honesty, and devotion.

***GURBANI VIDHYA CAMP 2023***
We are pleased to announce our second Gurbani Vidhya Camp, which will be running from 7-20th August at Gurdwara Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, Leicester. Last year we were blessed to go through the complete Paath Bodh of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji Maharaj. Following on, this year over the span of two weeks Vidhiarthis will have a chance to hear the Shudh Ucharan of Bhai Gurdas Ji's Vaars, with Vishraams and Uchaaran explained, while they follow with their Pothi Sahibs. 

We will be joined by various Gursikh Vidhvaans, including Sant Hari Singh Ji Randhawe Wale, Giani Satnaam Singh Ji Hanspur Wale, Ustad Jatinder Singh Ji (Nihung Santhia) and many soon to be announced. These Vidhvaans will be holding Katha workshops covering different Granths over the two weeks. There will be a special session daily by Sant Hari Singh Ji. 

Alongside, there will also be Kirtan (Jorri/Tanti Saaj) workshops and Shastar Vidhya Workshops (including horseriding sessions).

Dates:  7-20th August 2023
Venue: Gurdwara Guru Tegh Bahadur, 106 East Park Rd, Leicester LE5 4QB 
Times: 9 am - 3 pm daily

🌟 Exciting Announcement 🌟

We are thrilled to announce the birth of Khalsa Sports Club, a community-oriented initiative dedicated to promoting unity, athleticism, and the spirit of the Khalsa!

🏑 Embracing Tradition, Fostering Excellence 🥅

As proud members of the vibrant Sikh community, we believe in the power of sports to bring people together, inspire confidence, and develop skills that extend far beyond the playing field. Khalsa Sports Club is a platform where individuals of all ages can come together to cultivate a love for sports while embracing our rich cultural heritage.

👥 Join Our Family, Ignite Your Passion ⚡️

Whether you are a beginner or a seasoned athlete, we invite you to become part of our growing family! Our club offers a range of exciting sports programs, from field hockey to kabaddi, where you can unleash your potential, hone your skills, and create lifelong friendships. Under the expert guidance of our experienced coaches, athletes will have opportunities to compete at local and national levels.

🌍 Strengthening Our Community 💪

Khalsa Sports Club is not just about the competition; we are committed to giving back to our community. Through various outreach initiatives and partnerships, we aspire to promote a healthy lifestyle, provide sports education, and empower the youth. Join us in making a positive impact on society while having a blast doing what you love.

📢 Stay Tuned for Exciting Events! 🎉

Follow us to stay updated on our upcoming events, tournaments, and activities! From charity sports tournaments to youth development programs, there will be plenty of opportunities to get involved and make a difference.

🌐 Spread the Word! ✨

Tag your friends, family, and anyone interested in joining us on this exhilarating journey. Let's build a sports community that celebrates diversity, embraces inclusivity, and exemplifies the remarkable unity of the Khalsa.

🙌 Together, We Rise! 🙌

Sant Giani Gurbachan Singh Ji are a manifest form of Brahm (Akaal Purkh) who carried the task of learning and teaching Spiritual knowledge to Singhs throughout their life.

ਮੁਖੀ ਟਕਸਾਲ ਕੇ, ਜੋ ਰਚੀ ਦਸ਼ਮੇਸ਼ ਜੀ ਨੇ, ਅਰਥ ਗੁਰੂ ਗਿਰਾ ਕੇ, ਬਹੁ ਸਿੰਘਨ ਕੋ ਦਾਨ ਦੀਨ। 
Sant Ji were the 12th leader of the Damdami Taksal created by Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji Maharaaj. They taught the meanings of the Baani recited by our Guru Sahibaans and gave the gift of this knowledge to many students.

ਨਿਮ੍ਰਤਾ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਸਾਧੂ, ਚੇਤਨ ਬਿਲਾਸ ਹਰੀ, ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਰੰਗ ਰਾਚ ਰਹੇ, ਨਿਆਈ ਜਲ ਮਾਹਿ ਮੀਨ।
Sant Gurbachan Singh Ji (Chetan=Gur, Bilaas= Bachan and Hari= Lion/Singh) were a treasure of humbleness and remained in the colours of Akaal Purkh Waheguru similar to the love of a fish to water.

ਗਿਆਨ ਕੇ ਭੰਡਾਰ ਰੂਪ, ਦੈਵੀ ਗੁਣੋਂ ਕੇ ਸਰੂਪ, ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਸੇ ਸੰਪੰਨ, ਪਰਮੇਸਰ ਮੈਂ ਭਯੋ ਲੀਨ।
Sant Ji are the treasure of knowledge and are full of Religious qualities as well as being full of love and they became one with Akaal Purkh Waheguru Ji.
